title: Communication Patterns & Best Practices
description: Choose the right communication method and avoid common pitfalls.

slides.title: Choosing the Right Pattern
slides.content:
# Communication Cheat Sheet

| Scenario | Recommended Method |
|----------|-------------------|
| Parent → Child | Props |
| Child → Parent | Events (`$emit`) |
| Two‑way binding on a component | `v-model` (or `v-model:propName`) |
| Deep nesting, avoid prop drilling | Provide/Inject (for cross‑cutting concerns) |
| Sibling components | Lift state up to common parent |
| Global state (many components, complex) | Pinia (or Vuex) |

Always prefer explicit props/events over provide/inject for components that are directly related. Provide/Inject is for libraries and cross‑cutting features.

slides.title: Anti‑Patterns to Avoid
slides.content:
# Common Mistakes

- **Mutating props directly** – always use events to notify parent.
- **Using `$parent` or `$root`** – creates tight coupling and is hard to maintain.
- **Overusing provide/inject** – makes data flow hard to trace; use sparingly.
- **Too many global components** – prefer local registration for clarity.
- **Not validating props/events** – missing type checks leads to subtle bugs.

> 💡 **Pro Tip**: Keep components as **stateless** as possible. Move business logic to composables or stores.

quizData.question: What is the recommended way for sibling components to communicate?

options.text: Lift the shared state up to a common parent component
Use `$parent` to directly access the sibling

quizData.explanation: The typical approach is to lift state up to the closest common ancestor and pass it down via props, with events for updates.
